scope: Surviving1909 concrete tower with square base, octagonal tapered shaft/watchroom, gallery and current lantern/beacon/caged access ladder; narrow own footing/entry steps only. Separate former residences/ruins, prison and vaulted cistern excluded.

selectedOriginals.caption: Alcatraz Island, lighthouse
selectedOriginals.inspection: Full original inspected. Tall octagonal taper with shallow recessed facet panels, narrow high shaft light, octagonal sash watchroom and corbels, open dark gallery rail, cylindrical helical-glazed lantern and shallow roof/current beacon. Square base visible; separate ruined residences/cistern/retaining walls excluded.

selectedOriginals.caption: It is interesting how such a beautiful lighthouse ended up being interspersed through the prison buildings.  This tower was built around 1909 and was automated in 1963.
selectedOriginals.inspection: Full original inspected. Tower rises behind separate prison; projecting gallery and caged upper access ladder beside lantern. Adjacent cellhouse and ruins are context only.

additionalInspected.caption: Alcatraz lighthouse
additionalInspected.inspection: Full original inspected. Tall square base with broad recessed planes, large narrow rectangular barred sash and smaller horizontal light above; actual narrow door on adjoining face, three shallow entry steps. Octagonal tapered shaft and projecting watchroom/gallery. Surrounding fence, garden and lamp excluded.

additionalInspected.caption: Touring the cellhouse on Alcatraz Island on a very rainy day.
additionalInspected.artist: HarshLight from San Jose, CA, USA
additionalInspected.inspection: Full3456x5184 original inspected. Long recessed trapezoidal panels, small gridded shaft sash, upper gridded watchroom sash alternating with blind panels, projecting corbels/deck, cylindrical lantern/helical bars, conical metal roof and caged access ladder. Gray weathered concrete is natural, not brick.

additionalInspected.caption: Alcatraz lighthouse
additionalInspected.inspection: Full original close top inspected. Octagonal watchroom with tall central gridded sash and blind neighboring panels, angular gallery corbels, triple horizontal dark rail, cylindrical glazed lantern with diagonal/helical bars, shallow saucer/conical roof, short modern beacon and side ladder cage.

primarySources.type: 1910 original station inventory transcribed in USLHS archive
primarySources.review: Read1910 report: square base/octagonal balance, natural gray reinforced concrete; base13ft9in, parapet10ft8in; base-to-ventilator90ft2.25in. Cylindrical lantern7ft7.42in to glass,2ft11.5in glazed height, helical bars. Eleven varied windows/two doors in historic configuration. Former residences abutted two sides. Historical dimensions are control estimates, not certified current survey.

This is an approximate photographic exterior, not a measured current survey.

Five actual full local originals/40 thumbnails inspected. Sparse unseen rear shaft/base openings and door bearing are conservative interpretations. Eleven historic varied windows/two doors do not establish their exact present positions. Fine concrete damage and ironwork are generalized; no original photo pixels used as textures.

Independent original USGS ground remains unchanged. One-metre source/sampling cannot certify hidden foundations or current paving classification. Default coarse Earth terrain compatibility and whole-island scenery are not certified. Separate prison, residences/ruins, cistern, fences and lamps excluded.

Current exact height endpoints and rear sash/door bearings remain uncertain. Source-field context and shared flat placement checks are bounded evidence, not a survey, complete real island scene or navigation/collision guarantee.
